summary: Master mining ESG, community relations and social license with practical tools, reporting methods, and stakeholder exercises. Enrol now.
lede: Mining ESG and community relations training helps mining professionals structure social performance work at operating sites. It addresses the practical task of managing community concerns and documenting responses, with practice in stakeholder and social risk mapping, grievance mechanism design, and ESG evidence preparation. Participants also explore community engagement planning and reporting social performance to operational leaders.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for mining professionals who must manage community-facing issues, social performance data, and ESG reporting in live operational settings. It suits people who already work with stakeholder engagement, environmental impacts, grievance handling, or mine governance and now need stronger structure, tools, and reporting discipline. Community Relations Managers managing mine-community engagement and grievance response. ESG Managers building site-level social performance controls and disclosures. Sustainability Leads coordinating mining ESG reporting and assurance evidence. Social Performance Officers tracking stakeholder issues and local commitments. Mine Operations Managers handling community impacts and access constraints. Environmental Managers managing dust, water, and noise issues affecting trust. Resettlement Specialists supporting livelihood and compensation interface planning. Stakeholder Engagement Officers maintaining dialogue logs and consultation records. Corporate Affairs Managers briefing executives on reputation and social risk. Project Development Managers planning stakeholder engagement before mine expansion.
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop, a current mining or project example, and any available stakeholder register, grievance log, ESG report, or community engagement note from your work context. Familiarity with basic spreadsheets is helpful for the workshop exercises, especially when building maps, trackers, and reporting evidence packs.
